Write a Python function wrap(text, width) that word-wraps text into a list of lines. Words are the runs of non-whitespace characters (what str.split() with no arguments returns). Fill lines greedily: a word joins the current line, after one space, if the line's length plus 1 plus the word's length is at most width; otherwise the current line is finished and the word starts the next line. A word longer than width is first cut into pieces of exactly width characters (the last piece may be shorter), and each piece is then placed as a word by the same rule, so further words may follow the last piece on its line. Lines never have leading or trailing spaces. Return [] when text has no words. If width is less than 1, raise ValueError. Examples: wrap("the quick brown fox", 10) -> ["the quick", "brown fox"], wrap("abcdefghij", 4) -> ["abcd", "efgh", "ij"], wrap("", 5) -> [], wrap("a b", 0) raises ValueError.
